section
variable (body : Carry → TypedMachine tapes B)
    (next : Carry → B → Carry) (stop : Carry → B → Bool) (verdict : Carry → B → Bool)

/-- One round advances the loop by `cost i + 1` steps to the next round's

theorem TypedMachine.loopState_round (s₀ : Carry)
    (carry : Nat → Carry) (config : Nat → TypedConfiguration tapes B)
    (cost : Nat → Nat) (i : Nat)
    (hround : LoopRound body next stop carry config cost i) :
    (((TypedMachine.loopState body next stop verdict s₀).step^[cost i + 1])
        (TypedConfiguration.inLoop (carry i) (config i)) :
      TypedConfiguration tapes (Carry × B)) =
      TypedConfiguration.inLoop (carry (i + 1)) (config (i + 1)) := by

      (config i) (cost i) hv.fresh,

      hv.halts hround.keeps,
    hround.config_succ, hround.carry_succ]

/-- After `rounds` complete rounds the loop stands at round `rounds`.
The total cost is `loopCost cost rounds = Σ (cost i + 1)`: each round pays its
body plus the single re-entry step. -/
theorem TypedMachine.loopState_rounds (s₀ : Carry)
    (carry : Nat → Carry) (config : Nat → TypedConfiguration tapes B)
    (cost : Nat → Nat) (rounds : Nat)
    (hround : ∀ i, i < rounds → LoopRound body next stop carry config cost i) :
    (((TypedMachine.loopState body next stop verdict s₀).step^[
          loopCost cost rounds])
        (TypedConfiguration.inLoop (carry 0) (config 0)) :
      TypedConfiguration tapes (Carry × B)) =
      TypedConfiguration.inLoop (carry rounds) (config rounds) := by
  induction rounds with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ rounds ih =>
      rw [loopCost, Nat.add_comm (loopCost cost rounds) (cost rounds + 1),
        Function.iterate_add_apply,
        ih (fun i hi => hround i (Nat.lt_succ_of_lt hi)),
        TypedMachine.loopState_round body next stop verdict s₀ carry config cost
          rounds (hround rounds (Nat.lt_succ_self rounds))]

/-- **The loop as a subroutine.**  Given per-round records and a final round
that stops, the whole loop is a `HaltsExactly` obligation of cost
`loopCost cost rounds + a`, and therefore composes with `andThen`. -/
theorem TypedMachine.loopState_spec (s₀ : Carry)
    (carry : Nat → Carry) (config : Nat → TypedConfiguration tapes B)
    (cost : Nat → Nat) (rounds : Nat) (a : Nat) (v : Bool)
    (hround : ∀ i, i < rounds → LoopRound body next stop carry config cost i)
    (hexit : HaltsExactly (body (carry rounds)) (config rounds) a v)
    (hstop : stop (carry rounds)
      (((body (carry rounds)).step^[a]) (config rounds)).state = true)
    (hverdict : verdict (carry rounds)
      (((body (carry rounds)).step^[a]) (config rounds)).state = v) :
    HaltsExactly (TypedMachine.loopState body next stop verdict s₀)
      (TypedConfiguration.inLoop (carry 0) (config 0))
      (loopCost cost rounds + a) v := by
  have hrun :=
    TypedMachine.loopState_rounds body next stop verdict s₀ carry config cost
      rounds hround
  constructor
  · rw [Nat.add_comm, Function.iterate_add_apply, hrun,
      TypedMachine.loopState_iterate_body body next stop verdict s₀
        (carry rounds) (config rounds) a hexit.fresh,
      TypedMachine.loopState_result_stop body next stop verdict s₀
        (carry rounds) hexit.halts hstop, hverdict]
  · intro j hj
    rcases Nat.lt_or_ge j (loopCost cost rounds) with hlt | hge
    · -- inside the completed rounds
      clear hrun hexit hstop hverdict hj
      induction rounds with
      | zero => simp [loopCost] at hlt
      | succ rounds ih =>
          rcases Nat.lt_or_ge j (loopCost cost rounds) with hlt' | hge'
          · exact ih (fun i hi => hround i (Nat.lt_succ_of_lt hi)) hlt'
          · obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hge'
            have htlt : t < cost rounds + 1 := by
              rw [loopCost] at hlt; omega
            obtain ⟨v', hv'⟩ := (hround rounds (Nat.lt_succ_self rounds)).halts
            rw [ht, Nat.add_comm, Function.iterate_add_apply,
              TypedMachine.loopState_rounds body next stop verdict s₀ carry
                config cost rounds
                (fun i hi => hround i (Nat.lt_succ_of_lt hi))]
            exact TypedMachine.loopState_round_fresh body next stop verdict s₀
              (carry rounds) (config rounds) (cost rounds) v' hv'
              (hround rounds (Nat.lt_succ_self rounds)).keeps t htlt
    · obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hge
      have htlt : t < a := by omega
      rw [ht, Nat.add_comm, Function.iterate_add_apply, hrun]
      exact TypedMachine.loopState_pre_fresh body next stop verdict s₀
        (carry rounds) (config rounds) a v hexit t htlt

end

end SipserGacsLautemann
theorems.natural_language_statement:
`loopState`: a loop whose body is a family indexed by a loop-carried value.

`repeatUntilFalse` re-enters its body at the fixed `body.start`, so all control state is erased between rounds. That is deliberate — it is what forces loop counters onto the tapes, and it is why an *input-dependent* number of rounds is expressible at all. But it makes the combinator unable to express a **simulation**, whose rounds must carry the simulated machine's state $q$ from each round to the next. The same failure recurs one level down: a sweep that reads a symbol partway along must still know it when the sweep ends.

`loopState` closes this. The body is a family $\mathrm{body} : \mathrm{Carry} \to \mathrm{TypedMachine}$, so the carried value is a *parameter of the round's program* rather than something threaded at runtime — every dispatch inside a round receives it by construction. That is the same device that makes `andThenState` work, lifted from a single hand-off to an unbounded iteration. Taking the carried type to be trivial recovers `repeatUntilFalse` as the degenerate instance.

**The round record.** `LoopRound` packages, for round $i$, everything the induction over rounds needs: that the round's body halts on schedule, that the stopping condition does not fire, and the two equations locating the next round's carried value and configuration. Bundling these in one record rather than as loose conjuncts is what keeps the induction to a single hypothesis — the alternative is the sort of ad-hoc accumulation that produces unmaintainable proofs.

**The specification.** `loopState_spec` states that given per-round records and a final round that stops, the entire loop is one `HaltsExactly` obligation of cost

$$
\mathrm{loopCost}(c, r) + a \;=\; \Big(\sum_{i<r} (c_i + 1)\Big) + a ,
$$

each round paying its body plus a single re-entry step. Loops therefore remain first-class subroutines and nest inside `andThen` chains exactly as before, now while carrying state.

/-!
# `FiresExactly`, `readAct`, and the halting adapters

Module A of the merge_empty plan (`DESIGN_merge_empty_v2.md`).

Two spec formats coexist in the development: `HaltsExactly` speaks about a
machine's `result`, while `andThenState` composes on an **exit predicate over
states**.  The sweeps of the simulation will be loops used as the first
component of `andThenState`, so they need exit-firing specifications, not
halting ones.  `FiresExactly` is the common currency: a predicate on
configurations, first true at exactly time `t`.  Everything downstream is
stated in this form; `HaltsExactly` embeds into it.

The module also supplies `readAct` — the primitive that *reads* the symbols
under the heads, *acts* on them, and *remembers* what it read.  `act` acts but
forgets; `test` remembers one bit but cannot act; applying a simulated
machine's transition needs all three at once.

Finally, the bridge out: a `HaltsExactly` at exact time `t` yields
`acceptsWithin`/`rejectsWithin` at any bound `T ≥ t`, which is what
`DecidesInPolynomialTime` actually consumes.
-/

namespace SipserGacsLautemann

variable {tapes : Nat}

/-! ## The firing specification -/

/-- `pred` is first true at exactly time `t` along the orbit of `step` from
`c`. -/
structure FiresExactly {α : Type*} (pred : α → Bool) (step : α → α)
    (c : α) (t : Nat) : Prop where
  fires : pred ((step^[t]) c) = true
  fresh : ∀ j, j < t → pred ((step^[j]) c) = false

/-- The halting predicate of a machine, as a Boolean on configurations. -/
def haltPred {S : Type} (machine : TypedMachine tapes S) :
    TypedConfiguration tapes S → Bool :=
  fun c => (machine.result c.state).isSome

/-- `HaltsExactly` is a `FiresExactly` for the halting predicate. -/
theorem HaltsExactly.toFires {S : Type} {machine : TypedMachine tapes S}
    {c : TypedConfiguration tapes S} {t : Nat} {v : Bool}
    (h : HaltsExactly machine c t v) :
    FiresExactly (haltPred machine) machine.step c t := by
  constructor
  · simp [haltPred, h.halts]
  · intro j hj
    simp [haltPred, h.fresh j hj]

/-- An exit-firing spec for `M₁` composes with a halting spec for the
continuation — `HaltsExactly.andThenState` in `FiresExactly` clothing. -/
theorem FiresExactly.andThenState_halts {S₁ S₂ : Type}
    {M₁ : TypedMachine tapes S₁} {exit : S₁ → Bool}
    {M₂ : S₁ → TypedMachine tapes S₂}
    {c : TypedConfiguration tapes S₁} {a k : Nat} {v : Bool}
    (hf : FiresExactly (fun cfg => exit cfg.state) M₁.step c a)
    (h₂ : HaltsExactly (M₂ ((M₁.step^[a]) c).state)
      ((M₂ ((M₁.step^[a]) c).state).startCfg ((M₁.step^[a]) c).tape) k v) :
    HaltsExactly (M₁.andThenState exit M₂)
      (TypedConfiguration.inLeftState c) (a + 1 + k) v :=
  HaltsExactly.andThenState hf.fires hf.fresh h₂

/-! ## `readAct`: read, act, remember -/

/-- One step that reads the symbols under all heads, applies the induced
actions, and records a value computed from what it read.  Never halts on its
own; composed via `andThenState` with exit `Option.isSome`. -/
def TypedMachine.readAct {S : Type}
    (program :
      (Fin tapes → TapeSymbol) → S × (Fin tapes → TapeSymbol × HeadMove)) :
    TypedMachine tapes (Option S) where
  start := none
  transition := fun state symbols =>
    match state with
    | none => (some (program symbols).1, (program symbols).2)
    | some s => (some s, fun i => (symbols i, HeadMove.stay))
  result := fun _ => none

/-- After its single step, `readAct` records the value computed from the head
symbols and its tapes are the applied action. -/
theorem TypedMachine.readAct_run_one {S : Type}
    (program :
      (Fin tapes → TapeSymbol) → S × (Fin tapes → TapeSymbol × HeadMove))
    (tape : Fin tapes → Tape) :
    ((TypedMachine.readAct program).step^[1])
        ((TypedMachine.readAct program).startCfg tape) =
      ⟨some (program (fun i => (tape i).head)).1,
        applyAction tape (fun symbols => (program symbols).2)⟩ := by
  rw [Function.iterate_one]
  rfl

/-- `readAct`'s exit predicate fires at exactly time `1`. -/
theorem TypedMachine.readAct_fires {S : Type}
    (program :
      (Fin tapes → TapeSymbol) → S × (Fin tapes → TapeSymbol × HeadMove))
    (tape : Fin tapes → Tape) :
    FiresExactly (fun c => c.state.isSome)
      (TypedMachine.readAct program).step
      ((TypedMachine.readAct program).startCfg tape) 1 := by
  constructor
  · rw [TypedMachine.readAct_run_one]
    rfl
  · intro j hj
    have hj0 : j = 0 := by omega
    subst hj0
    rfl

/-! ## Out of `HaltsExactly`, into the time-bounded world -/

theorem TypedMachine.startCfg_ofBits {S : Type} (machine : TypedMachine tapes S)
    (input : Fin tapes → List Bool) :
    machine.startCfg (fun i => Tape.ofBits (input i)) =
      machine.initialConfiguration input := rfl

/-- A machine that halts exactly at `t` still reports the same verdict at any
later bound: halting states absorb. -/
theorem HaltsExactly.result_run_of_le {S : Type} {machine : TypedMachine tapes S}
    {input : Fin tapes → List Bool} {t : Nat} {v : Bool}
    (h : HaltsExactly machine (machine.initialConfiguration input) t v)
    {T : Nat} (hle : t ≤ T) :
    machine.result ((machine.run input T).state) = some v := by
  obtain ⟨e, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hle
  have ht : machine.result ((machine.run input t).state) = some v := by
    rw [TypedMachine.run_eq_iterate_step]
    exact h.halts
  rw [machine.run_add_eq_of_result_run_eq_some input t e ht]
  exact ht

/-- The accepting half of the `DecidesInPolynomialTime` interface, from an
exact halting spec. -/
theorem HaltsExactly.toMachine_acceptsWithin {S : Type} [Fintype S]
    {machine : TypedMachine tapes S} {input : Fin tapes → List Bool} {t : Nat}
    (h : HaltsExactly machine (machine.initialConfiguration input) t true)
    {T : Nat} (hle : t ≤ T) :
    machine.toMachine.acceptsWithin input T := by
  rw [TypedMachine.toMachine_acceptsWithin_iff]
  exact h.result_run_of_le hle

/-- The rejecting half. -/
theorem HaltsExactly.toMachine_rejectsWithin {S : Type} [Fintype S]
    {machine : TypedMachine tapes S} {input : Fin tapes → List Bool} {t : Nat}
    (h : HaltsExactly machine (machine.initialConfiguration input) t false)
    {T : Nat} (hle : t ≤ T) :
    machine.toMachine.rejectsWithin input T := by
  rw [TypedMachine.toMachine_rejectsWithin_iff]
  exact h.result_run_of_le hle

end SipserGacsLautemann

namespace SipserGacsLautemann

theorem merge_empty_scratch_tapes {tapes : Nat} (scratch : Nat)
    (predicate : (Fin tapes → List Bool) → Prop)
    (hdecides : DecidesInPolynomialTimeWithScratch (scratch + 2) predicate) :
    DecidesInPolynomialTimeWithScratch (scratch + 1) predicate := by sorry
theorems.natural_language_statement:
A predicate decidable in polynomial time with $s+2$ blank work tapes is decidable in polynomial time with $s+1$.

This is the easy half of tape elimination, and it is easy for one specific reason: **both tapes being merged start empty**, so there is nothing to gather and no existing content to re-encode. The two may simply be hosted as two tracks of a single tape, each position carrying one cell of each track together with a flag recording whether that track's head is there. Since exactly one physical head must serve two virtual heads, each simulated step costs a sweep of the region written so far; that region grows by at most one position per step, so the overhead is quadratic — comfortably polynomial.

The statement should not be mistaken for a warm-up exercise. Avoiding the re-encoding phase does not avoid the per-step simulation argument: the flags, the sweeps, and the invariant relating the simulated configuration to the physical one are all still required. It is the full construction minus one phase.

Avoiding the re-encoding phase does not avoid the per-step simulation argument: the flags, the sweeps, and the invariant relating the simulated configuration to the physical one are all still required. It is the full construction minus one phase.

import Definitions.Def_sgl_state_algebra

/-!
# Two virtual tapes on one physical tape

The representation on which scratch-tape elimination rests.  A physical tape is
read as a list of **blocks**, each holding one cell of each of two virtual
tracks together with a flag marking whether that track's head is here.

The design question this module answers is whether the representation survives
contact with `Tape`, which is a zipper `⟨left, head, right⟩` with no absolute
coordinate.  Two virtual tapes must be aligned *by position*, and a zipper does
not carry one — so the correspondence is stated in the direction
blocks → tapes, where the flag supplies the missing coordinate: the projected
tape is split at the flagged block.

`trackTape_write` and `trackTape_moveRight` are the two lemmas that matter.
They say that writing at the flagged block implements `Tape.write`, and moving
the flag one block right implements `Tape.move .right`, on the projected tape.
If these hold, block-level programs implement tape-level semantics and the
per-step simulation lemma has a target to aim at.
-/

namespace SipserGacsLautemann

/-- One position of the physical tape: a cell of each track, plus each track's
head flag. -/
structure Block where
  symA : TapeSymbol
  flagA : Bool
  symB : TapeSymbol
  flagB : Bool

/-- An untouched position. -/
def Block.blank : Block := ⟨TapeSymbol.blank, false, TapeSymbol.blank, false⟩

/-- Project a block list onto a track, as a plain symbol list. -/
def trackSyms (pick : Block → TapeSymbol) (blocks : List Block) :
    List TapeSymbol :=
  blocks.map pick

/-- The virtual tape carried by one track: the projected symbols, split at the
flagged block.  The flag is what supplies the absolute coordinate that the
zipper representation lacks.

`before` is stored **nearest-block-first**, matching `Tape.left`'s own
convention.  Storing it in reading order and reversing looks more natural and is
wrong: `Tape.move .right` prepends the old head to `left`, so the two orders
disagree the moment the head moves. -/
def trackTape (pick : Block → TapeSymbol) (before : List Block) (cur : Block)
    (after : List Block) : Tape :=
  ⟨trackSyms pick before, pick cur, trackSyms pick after⟩

/-- Writing at the flagged block implements `Tape.write` on the projected
tape. -/
theorem trackTape_write (pick : Block → TapeSymbol) (set : TapeSymbol → Block → Block)
    (hset : ∀ s b, pick (set s b) = s)
    (before : List Block) (cur : Block) (after : List Block) (s : TapeSymbol) :
    trackTape pick before (set s cur) after =
      Tape.write (trackTape pick before cur after) s := by
  simp [trackTape, Tape.write, hset]

/-- Moving the flag one block right implements `Tape.move .right`, when there is
a next block. -/
theorem trackTape_moveRight (pick : Block → TapeSymbol)
    (before : List Block) (cur : Block) (nxt : Block) (after : List Block) :
    trackTape pick (cur :: before) nxt after =
      Tape.move (trackTape pick before cur (nxt :: after)) HeadMove.right := by
  simp [trackTape, trackSyms, Tape.move]

/-- Moving the flag one block left implements `Tape.move .left`, when there is a
previous block. -/
theorem trackTape_moveLeft (pick : Block → TapeSymbol)
    (before : List Block) (prv : Block) (cur : Block) (after : List Block) :
    trackTape pick before prv (cur :: after) =
      Tape.move (trackTape pick (prv :: before) cur after) HeadMove.left := by
  simp [trackTape, trackSyms, Tape.move]

/-- At the right edge the region must be extended with a blank block; doing so
still implements `Tape.move .right`. -/
theorem trackTape_moveRight_pad (pick : Block → TapeSymbol)
    (hblank : pick Block.blank = TapeSymbol.blank)
    (before : List Block) (cur : Block) :
    trackTape pick (cur :: before) Block.blank [] =
      Tape.move (trackTape pick before cur []) HeadMove.right := by
  simp [trackTape, trackSyms, Tape.move, hblank]

/-- And at the left edge. -/
theorem trackTape_moveLeft_pad (pick : Block → TapeSymbol)
    (hblank : pick Block.blank = TapeSymbol.blank)
    (cur : Block) (after : List Block) :
    trackTape pick [] Block.blank (cur :: after) =
      Tape.move (trackTape pick [] cur after) HeadMove.left := by
  simp [trackTape, trackSyms, Tape.move, hblank]

/-! ## The two tracks

Both virtual tapes are projections of the *same* block list, differing only in
which field is read and which flag is followed.  Everything above applies to
each track by instantiation, so the two tapes cost one set of lemmas rather
than two. -/

def Block.setA (s : TapeSymbol) (b : Block) : Block := { b with symA := s }
def Block.setB (s : TapeSymbol) (b : Block) : Block := { b with symB := s }

theorem Block.symA_setA (s : TapeSymbol) (b : Block) :
    Block.symA (Block.setA s b) = s := rfl
theorem Block.symB_setB (s : TapeSymbol) (b : Block) :
    Block.symB (Block.setB s b) = s := rfl

/-- Writing on track A leaves track B's projection untouched: the two virtual
tapes are independent even though they share a block list. -/
theorem trackTape_setA_symB (before : List Block) (cur : Block)
    (after : List Block) (s : TapeSymbol) :
    trackTape Block.symB before (Block.setA s cur) after =
      trackTape Block.symB before cur after := by
  simp [trackTape, Block.setA]

theorem trackTape_setB_symA (before : List Block) (cur : Block)
    (after : List Block) (s : TapeSymbol) :
    trackTape Block.symA before (Block.setB s cur) after =
      trackTape Block.symA before cur after := by
  simp [trackTape, Block.setB]

end SipserGacsLautemann

theorems.definition:
import Definitions.Def_sgl_scratch_tapes

/-!
# Continuing on the state reached

`andThen` branches on a **`Bool`**, because the model's `result : State → Option
Bool` returns exactly one bit.  That is enough for control flow but not for
carrying *data* between subroutines: a simulation has to hand the simulated
machine's state — a `Fin states` — from the subroutine that reads the tape
symbols to the one that applies the transition.

`andThenState` closes that gap.  It runs `M₁` until it enters a state satisfying
`exit`, then continues with `M₂` applied to *that state*, so an arbitrary finite
amount of information crosses the boundary in the control rather than on a tape.

Structurally it is the same three-part argument as `andThen`: mirror `M₁` while
it has not exited, one hand-off step, then mirror the continuation.
-/

namespace SipserGacsLautemann

variable {tapes : Nat} {S₁ S₂ : Type}

/-- Run `M₁` until it reaches an `exit` state, then continue with `M₂` applied to
that state.  While in the first phase the composite mirrors `M₁` exactly,
including its stutter after halting. -/
def TypedMachine.andThenState (M₁ : TypedMachine tapes S₁) (exit : S₁ → Bool)
    (M₂ : S₁ → TypedMachine tapes S₂) :
    TypedMachine tapes (S₁ ⊕ S₁ × S₂) where
  start := Sum.inl M₁.start
  transition := fun state symbols =>
    match state with
    | Sum.inl s =>
        if exit s then
          (Sum.inr (s, (M₂ s).start), fun i => (symbols i, HeadMove.stay))
        else
          match M₁.result s with
          | some _ => (Sum.inl s, fun i => (symbols i, HeadMove.stay))
          | none =>
              let action := M₁.transition s symbols
              (Sum.inl action.1, action.2)
    | Sum.inr (s, q) =>
        let action := (M₂ s).transition q symbols
        (Sum.inr (s, action.1), action.2)
  result := fun state =>
    match state with
    | Sum.inl _ => none
    | Sum.inr (s, q) => (M₂ s).result q

/-- First-phase configurations of an `andThenState` composite. -/
def TypedConfiguration.inLeftState (c : TypedConfiguration tapes S₁) :
    TypedConfiguration tapes (S₁ ⊕ S₁ × S₂) :=
  ⟨Sum.inl c.state, c.tape⟩

/-- Second-phase configurations, tagged with the state that was handed over. -/
def TypedConfiguration.inRightState (s : S₁) (c : TypedConfiguration tapes S₂) :
    TypedConfiguration tapes (S₁ ⊕ S₁ × S₂) :=
  ⟨Sum.inr (s, c.state), c.tape⟩

theorem TypedMachine.andThenState_result_inLeftState
    (M₁ : TypedMachine tapes S₁) (exit : S₁ → Bool)
    (M₂ : S₁ → TypedMachine tapes S₂) (c : TypedConfiguration tapes S₁) :
    (M₁.andThenState exit M₂).result
      (TypedConfiguration.inLeftState (S₂ := S₂) c).state = none := rfl

/-- Before the exit condition fires the composite mirrors `M₁` step for step. -/
theorem TypedMachine.andThenState_iterate_left
    (M₁ : TypedMachine tapes S₁) (exit : S₁ → Bool)
    (M₂ : S₁ → TypedMachine tapes S₂) (c : TypedConfiguration tapes S₁) :
    ∀ k : Nat,
      (∀ j, j < k → exit ((M₁.step^[j]) c).state = false) →
      (((M₁.andThenState exit M₂).step^[k])
          (TypedConfiguration.inLeftState c) :
        TypedConfiguration tapes (S₁ ⊕ S₁ × S₂)) =
        TypedConfiguration.inLeftState ((M₁.step^[k]) c) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero => intro _; rfl
  | succ k ih =>
      intro hfresh
      have hprev : ∀ j, j < k → exit ((M₁.step^[j]) c).state = false :=
        fun j hj => hfresh j (Nat.lt_succ_of_lt hj)
      rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply', Function.iterate_succ_apply', ih hprev]
      have hno : exit ((M₁.step^[k]) c).state = false :=
        hfresh k (Nat.lt_succ_self k)
      cases hres : M₁.result ((M₁.step^[k]) c).state with
      | some r =>
          simp [TypedMachine.step, TypedMachine.andThenState,
            TypedConfiguration.inLeftState, hno, hres,
            Tape.write_head_self, Tape.move]
      | none =>
          simp [TypedMachine.step, TypedMachine.andThenState,
            TypedConfiguration.inLeftState, hno, hres]

/-- The hand-off: the state reached selects the continuation and the tapes cross
untouched. -/
theorem TypedMachine.andThenState_step_handoff
    (M₁ : TypedMachine tapes S₁) (exit : S₁ → Bool)
    (M₂ : S₁ → TypedMachine tapes S₂) {c : TypedConfiguration tapes S₁}
    (hexit : exit c.state = true) :
    (M₁.andThenState exit M₂).step (TypedConfiguration.inLeftState c) =
      TypedConfiguration.inRightState c.state
        ⟨(M₂ c.state).start, c.tape⟩ := by
  simp [TypedMachine.step, TypedMachine.andThenState,
    TypedConfiguration.inLeftState, TypedConfiguration.inRightState, hexit,
    Tape.write_head_self, Tape.move]

/-- After the hand-off the composite mirrors the continuation. -/
theorem TypedMachine.andThenState_iterate_right
    (M₁ : TypedMachine tapes S₁) (exit : S₁ → Bool)
    (M₂ : S₁ → TypedMachine tapes S₂) (s : S₁)
    (c : TypedConfiguration tapes S₂) :
    ∀ k : Nat,
      (((M₁.andThenState exit M₂).step^[k])
          (TypedConfiguration.inRightState s c) :
        TypedConfiguration tapes (S₁ ⊕ S₁ × S₂)) =
        TypedConfiguration.inRightState s (((M₂ s).step^[k]) c) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ k ih =>
      rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply', Function.iterate_succ_apply', ih]
      cases hres : (M₂ s).result (((M₂ s).step^[k]) c).state with
      | some r =>
          simp [TypedMachine.step, TypedMachine.andThenState,
            TypedConfiguration.inRightState, hres]
      | none =>
          simp [TypedMachine.step, TypedMachine.andThenState,
            TypedConfiguration.inRightState, hres]

/-- **Keystone, data-carrying form.**  If `M₁` first exits at time `a` in state
`s`, the composite after `a + 1 + k` steps is `M₂ s` after `k` steps on `M₁`'s
output tapes. -/
theorem TypedMachine.andThenState_iterate
    (M₁ : TypedMachine tapes S₁) (exit : S₁ → Bool)
    (M₂ : S₁ → TypedMachine tapes S₂) (c : TypedConfiguration tapes S₁) (a : Nat)
    (hexit : exit ((M₁.step^[a]) c).state = true)
    (hfresh : ∀ j, j < a → exit ((M₁.step^[j]) c).state = false) (k : Nat) :
    (((M₁.andThenState exit M₂).step^[a + 1 + k])
        (TypedConfiguration.inLeftState c) :
      TypedConfiguration tapes (S₁ ⊕ S₁ × S₂)) =
      TypedConfiguration.inRightState ((M₁.step^[a]) c).state
        (((M₂ ((M₁.step^[a]) c).state).step^[k])
          ⟨(M₂ ((M₁.step^[a]) c).state).start, ((M₁.step^[a]) c).tape⟩) := by
  rw [show a + 1 + k = k + (1 + a) by omega,
    Function.iterate_add_apply, Function.iterate_add_apply,
    Function.iterate_one]
  rw [M₁.andThenState_iterate_left exit M₂ c a hfresh]
  rw [M₁.andThenState_step_handoff exit M₂ hexit]
  exact M₁.andThenState_iterate_right exit M₂ _ _ k

/-- **Specs compose, carrying state.**  The counterpart of
`HaltsExactly.andThen` for data-carrying hand-off. -/
theorem HaltsExactly.andThenState
    {M₁ : TypedMachine tapes S₁} {exit : S₁ → Bool}
    {M₂ : S₁ → TypedMachine tapes S₂} {c : TypedConfiguration tapes S₁}
    {a k : Nat} {v : Bool}
    (hexit : exit ((M₁.step^[a]) c).state = true)
    (hfresh : ∀ j, j < a → exit ((M₁.step^[j]) c).state = false)
    (h₂ : HaltsExactly (M₂ ((M₁.step^[a]) c).state)
      ((M₂ ((M₁.step^[a]) c).state).startCfg ((M₁.step^[a]) c).tape) k v) :
    HaltsExactly (M₁.andThenState exit M₂)
      (TypedConfiguration.inLeftState c) (a + 1 + k) v := by
  constructor
  · rw [M₁.andThenState_iterate exit M₂ c a hexit hfresh k]
    exact h₂.halts
  · intro j hj
    rcases Nat.lt_or_ge j (a + 1) with hsmall | hbig
    · have hfr : ∀ i, i < j → exit ((M₁.step^[i]) c).state = false :=
        fun i hi => hfresh i (by omega)
      rw [M₁.andThenState_iterate_left exit M₂ c j hfr]
      exact M₁.andThenState_result_inLeftState exit M₂ _
    · obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hbig
      have hmk : m < k := by omega
      rw [hm, M₁.andThenState_iterate exit M₂ c a hexit hfresh m]
      exact h₂.fresh m hmk

end SipserGacsLautemann
theorems.natural_language_statement:
Continuing on the state reached: the data-carrying counterpart of `andThen`.

`andThen` branches on a **Boolean**, because the model's `result : State → Option Bool` returns exactly one bit. That is enough for control flow but not for carrying *data* between subroutines. A simulation must hand the simulated machine's state — an element of `Fin\ states` — from the subroutine that reads the tape symbols to the one that applies the transition, and one bit will not do it.

theorems.definition:
import Definitions.Def_sgl_scratch_tapes

/-!
# Continuing on the state reached

`andThen` branches on a **`Bool`**, because the model's `result : State → Option
Bool` returns exactly one bit.  That is enough for control flow but not for
carrying *data* between subroutines: a simulation has to hand the simulated
machine's state — a `Fin states` — from the subroutine that reads the tape
symbols to the one that applies the transition.

`andThenState` closes that gap.  It runs `M₁` until it enters a state satisfying
`exit`, then continues with `M₂` applied to *that state*, so an arbitrary finite
amount of information crosses the boundary in the control rather than on a tape.

Structurally it is the same three-part argument as `andThen`: mirror `M₁` while
it has not exited, one hand-off step, then mirror the continuation.
-/

namespace SipserGacsLautemann

variable {tapes : Nat} {S₁ S₂ : Type}

/-- Run `M₁` until it reaches an `exit` state, then continue with `M₂` applied to
that state.  While in the first phase the composite mirrors `M₁` exactly,
including its stutter after halting. -/
def TypedMachine.andThenState (M₁ : TypedMachine tapes S₁) (exit : S₁ → Bool)
    (M₂ : S₁ → TypedMachine tapes S₂) :
    TypedMachine tapes (S₁ ⊕ S₁ × S₂) where
  start := Sum.inl M₁.start
  transition := fun state symbols =>
    match state with
    | Sum.inl s =>
        if exit s then
          (Sum.inr (s, (M₂ s).start), fun i => (symbols i, HeadMove.stay))
        else
          match M₁.result s with
          | some _ => (Sum.inl s, fun i => (symbols i, HeadMove.stay))
          | none =>
              let action := M₁.transition s symbols
              (Sum.inl action.1, action.2)
    | Sum.inr (s, q) =>
        let action := (M₂ s).transition q symbols
        (Sum.inr (s, action.1), action.2)
  result := fun state =>
    match state with
    | Sum.inl _ => none
    | Sum.inr (s, q) => (M₂ s).result q

/-- First-phase configurations of an `andThenState` composite. -/
def TypedConfiguration.inLeftState (c : TypedConfiguration tapes S₁) :
    TypedConfiguration tapes (S₁ ⊕ S₁ × S₂) :=
  ⟨Sum.inl c.state, c.tape⟩

/-- Second-phase configurations, tagged with the state that was handed over. -/
def TypedConfiguration.inRightState (s : S₁) (c : TypedConfiguration tapes S₂) :
    TypedConfiguration tapes (S₁ ⊕ S₁ × S₂) :=
  ⟨Sum.inr (s, c.state), c.tape⟩

theorem TypedMachine.andThenState_result_inLeftState
    (M₁ : TypedMachine tapes S₁) (exit : S₁ → Bool)
    (M₂ : S₁ → TypedMachine tapes S₂) (c : TypedConfiguration tapes S₁) :
    (M₁.andThenState exit M₂).result
      (TypedConfiguration.inLeftState (S₂ := S₂) c).state = none := rfl

/-- Before the exit condition fires the composite mirrors `M₁` step for step. -/
theorem TypedMachine.andThenState_iterate_left
    (M₁ : TypedMachine tapes S₁) (exit : S₁ → Bool)
    (M₂ : S₁ → TypedMachine tapes S₂) (c : TypedConfiguration tapes S₁) :
    ∀ k : Nat,
      (∀ j, j < k → exit ((M₁.step^[j]) c).state = false) →
      (((M₁.andThenState exit M₂).step^[k])
          (TypedConfiguration.inLeftState c) :
        TypedConfiguration tapes (S₁ ⊕ S₁ × S₂)) =
        TypedConfiguration.inLeftState ((M₁.step^[k]) c) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero => intro _; rfl
  | succ k ih =>
      intro hfresh
      have hprev : ∀ j, j < k → exit ((M₁.step^[j]) c).state = false :=
        fun j hj => hfresh j (Nat.lt_succ_of_lt hj)
      rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply', Function.iterate_succ_apply', ih hprev]
      have hno : exit ((M₁.step^[k]) c).state = false :=
        hfresh k (Nat.lt_succ_self k)
      cases hres : M₁.result ((M₁.step^[k]) c).state with
      | some r =>
          simp [TypedMachine.step, TypedMachine.andThenState,
            TypedConfiguration.inLeftState, hno, hres,
            Tape.write_head_self, Tape.move]
      | none =>
          simp [TypedMachine.step, TypedMachine.andThenState,
            TypedConfiguration.inLeftState, hno, hres]

/-- The hand-off: the state reached selects the continuation and the tapes cross
untouched. -/
theorem TypedMachine.andThenState_step_handoff
    (M₁ : TypedMachine tapes S₁) (exit : S₁ → Bool)
    (M₂ : S₁ → TypedMachine tapes S₂) {c : TypedConfiguration tapes S₁}
    (hexit : exit c.state = true) :
    (M₁.andThenState exit M₂).step (TypedConfiguration.inLeftState c) =
      TypedConfiguration.inRightState c.state
        ⟨(M₂ c.state).start, c.tape⟩ := by
  simp [TypedMachine.step, TypedMachine.andThenState,
    TypedConfiguration.inLeftState, TypedConfiguration.inRightState, hexit,
    Tape.write_head_self, Tape.move]

/-- After the hand-off the composite mirrors the continuation. -/
theorem TypedMachine.andThenState_iterate_right
    (M₁ : TypedMachine tapes S₁) (exit : S₁ → Bool)
    (M₂ : S₁ → TypedMachine tapes S₂) (s : S₁)
    (c : TypedConfiguration tapes S₂) :
    ∀ k : Nat,
      (((M₁.andThenState exit M₂).step^[k])
          (TypedConfiguration.inRightState s c) :
        TypedConfiguration tapes (S₁ ⊕ S₁ × S₂)) =
        TypedConfiguration.inRightState s (((M₂ s).step^[k]) c) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ k ih =>
      rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply', Function.iterate_succ_apply', ih]
      cases hres : (M₂ s).result (((M₂ s).step^[k]) c).state with
      | some r =>
          simp [TypedMachine.step, TypedMachine.andThenState,
            TypedConfiguration.inRightState, hres]
      | none =>
          simp [TypedMachine.step, TypedMachine.andThenState,
            TypedConfiguration.inRightState, hres]

/-- **Keystone, data-carrying form.**  If `M₁` first exits at time `a` in state
`s`, the composite after `a + 1 + k` steps is `M₂ s` after `k` steps on `M₁`'s
output tapes. -/
theorem TypedMachine.andThenState_iterate
    (M₁ : TypedMachine tapes S₁) (exit : S₁ → Bool)
    (M₂ : S₁ → TypedMachine tapes S₂) (c : TypedConfiguration tapes S₁) (a : Nat)
    (hexit : exit ((M₁.step^[a]) c).state = true)
    (hfresh : ∀ j, j < a → exit ((M₁.step^[j]) c).state = false) (k : Nat) :
    (((M₁.andThenState exit M₂).step^[a + 1 + k])
        (TypedConfiguration.inLeftState c) :
      TypedConfiguration tapes (S₁ ⊕ S₁ × S₂)) =
      TypedConfiguration.inRightState ((M₁.step^[a]) c).state
        (((M₂ ((M₁.step^[a]) c).state).step^[k])
          ⟨(M₂ ((M₁.step^[a]) c).state).start, ((M₁.step^[a]) c).tape⟩) := by
  rw [show a + 1 + k = k + (1 + a) by omega,
    Function.iterate_add_apply, Function.iterate_add_apply,
    Function.iterate_one]
  rw [M₁.andThenState_iterate_left exit M₂ c a hfresh]
  rw [M₁.andThenState_step_handoff exit M₂ hexit]
  exact M₁.andThenState_iterate_right exit M₂ _ _ k

/-- **Specs compose, carrying state.**  The counterpart of
`HaltsExactly.andThen` for data-carrying hand-off. -/
theorem HaltsExactly.andThenState
    {M₁ : TypedMachine tapes S₁} {exit : S₁ → Bool}
    {M₂ : S₁ → TypedMachine tapes S₂} {c : TypedConfiguration tapes S₁}
    {a k : Nat} {v : Bool}
    (hexit : exit ((M₁.step^[a]) c).state = true)
    (hfresh : ∀ j, j < a → exit ((M₁.step^[j]) c).state = false)
    (h₂ : HaltsExactly (M₂ ((M₁.step^[a]) c).state)
      ((M₂ ((M₁.step^[a]) c).state).startCfg ((M₁.step^[a]) c).tape) k v) :
    HaltsExactly (M₁.andThenState exit M₂)
      (TypedConfiguration.inLeftState c) (a + 1 + k) v := by
  constructor
  · rw [M₁.andThenState_iterate exit M₂ c a hexit hfresh k]
    exact h₂.halts
  · intro j hj
    rcases Nat.lt_or_ge j (a + 1) with hsmall | hbig
    · have hfr : ∀ i, i < j → exit ((M₁.step^[i]) c).state = false :=
        fun i hi => hfresh i (by omega)
      rw [M₁.andThenState_iterate_left exit M₂ c j hfr]
      exact M₁.andThenState_result_inLeftState exit M₂ _
    · obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hbig
      have hmk : m < k := by omega
      rw [hm, M₁.andThenState_iterate exit M₂ c a hexit hfresh m]
      exact h₂.fresh m hmk

end SipserGacsLautemann

namespace SipserGacsLautemann

theorem scratch_tape_provisioning {tapes : Nat} (scratch : Nat)
    (predicate : (Fin tapes → List Bool) → Prop)
    (hdecides : DecidesInPolynomialTimeWithScratch scratch predicate) :
    DecidesInPolynomialTime predicate := by sorry

theorems.natural_language_statement:
A predicate decidable in polynomial time by a machine granted any fixed number of blank work tapes is decidable in polynomial time in the mission's own sense, with no extra tapes at all.

This is the licence to program the machine model normally. As stated, `DecidesInPolynomialTime` hands a construction exactly as many tapes as the predicate has arguments, every one of them already holding a piece of the input; there is nowhere to put a counter, an intermediate string, or the answer of a subroutine. With this theorem one may write a machine that helps itself to as much blank working storage as convenient and still conclude membership in the class.

The statement is the natural notion of a *conservative* extension: at zero scratch tapes the hypothesis is literally the conclusion, and each additional tape is removed by the classical multitape simulation at polynomial cost.

namespace SipserGacsLautemann

theorem eliminate_one_scratch_tape {tapes : Nat} (scratch : Nat)
    (predicate : (Fin tapes → List Bool) → Prop)
    (hdecides : DecidesInPolynomialTimeWithScratch (scratch + 1) predicate) :

theorems.natural_language_statement:
A predicate decidable in polynomial time by a machine granted $s+1$ blank work tapes is decidable in polynomial time by one granted only $s$.

This is the tape-reduction step of the classical multitape simulation, specialized to a model whose tapes are fixed in number and preloaded with the input. The one tape being removed starts empty, so nothing has to be gathered: its contents may be hosted inside the blank region lying to the left of the input on a surviving tape, provided the simulating machine tracks that tape's head position. Because the alphabet has only the three symbols blank, $0$ and $1$, a head position cannot be marked by a fresh symbol and must instead be recorded by widening each simulated cell into a fixed-size block of physical cells.

Only a polynomial overhead is required, so the crude simulation suffices: each simulated step costs a sweep of the region used so far, and the region grows by at most one cell per step, giving a quadratic blow-up in the running time.

This is the single obstruction standing between the mission's machine model and ordinary structured programming. Iterating it discharges any number of work tapes, so it is the only theorem needed for full scratch provisioning — and it is needed independently of this mission, since without it the model cannot even express that polynomial time is closed under intersection.

import Definitions.Def_sgl_vote_fold

/-!
# Scratch tapes

`DecidesInPolynomialTime` on `Fin k → List Bool` supplies exactly `k` tapes,
every one of them preloaded with a component of the input.  There is no blank
work tape anywhere in the model, and nothing in the development provides one:
`encodedSimulation` preserves the tape count, and
`decidesInPolynomialTime_add_unused_tape` runs the other way, adding a tape to
the *input* rather than handing out scratch.

That is a hard obstruction rather than an inconvenience.  One of the mission's
open frontier obligations asks for a `TypedMachine 3` that simulates a
`Machine 4`, so tape multiplexing is forced by the statement itself.  More
broadly, without scratch one cannot even show `P` closed under intersection:
running a second machine requires somewhere to record the first one's answer.

This module introduces the missing notion and reduces it to a single theorem.
`DecidesInPolynomialTimeWithScratch scratch P` is decidability by a machine with
`scratch` extra tapes that start empty.  The provisioning theorem — that this
implies ordinary `DecidesInPolynomialTime` — then follows by induction from the
elimination of **one** blank tape, so all the difficulty is concentrated in that
single step.
-/

namespace SipserGacsLautemann

variable {tapes : Nat}

/-- An input tuple padded with `scratch` empty tapes. -/
def withScratch (scratch : Nat) (input : Fin tapes → List Bool) :
    Fin (tapes + scratch) → List Bool :=
  fun i => if h : i.val < tapes then input ⟨i.val, h⟩ else []

@[simp] theorem withScratch_zero (input : Fin tapes → List Bool) :
    withScratch 0 input = input := by
  funext i
  have h : i.val < tapes := i.isLt
  simp [withScratch, h]

/-- Decidability in polynomial time by a machine granted `scratch` extra tapes,
each of which starts empty.  For `scratch = 0` this is exactly
`DecidesInPolynomialTime`. -/
def DecidesInPolynomialTimeWithScratch (scratch : Nat)
    (predicate : (Fin tapes → List Bool) → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ (states : Nat) (machine : Machine (tapes + scratch) states) (time : Nat → Nat),
    PolynomiallyBounded time ∧
      ∀ input : Fin tapes → List Bool,
        (machine.acceptsWithin (withScratch scratch input)
            (time (totalInputLength (withScratch scratch input))) ↔
          predicate input) ∧
        (machine.rejectsWithin (withScratch scratch input)
            (time (totalInputLength (withScratch scratch input))) ↔
          ¬predicate input)

/-- With no scratch tapes the notion collapses to the mission's own. -/
theorem decidesInPolynomialTimeWithScratch_zero
    (predicate : (Fin tapes → List Bool) → Prop) :
    DecidesInPolynomialTimeWithScratch 0 predicate ↔
      DecidesInPolynomialTime predicate := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨states, machine, time, htime, hcorrect⟩
    refine ⟨states, machine, time, htime, ?_⟩
    intro input
    have h := hcorrect input
    rwa [withScratch_zero] at h
  · rintro ⟨states, machine, time, htime, hcorrect⟩
    refine ⟨states, machine, time, htime, ?_⟩
    intro input
    have h := hcorrect input
    rwa [withScratch_zero]

end SipserGacsLautemann
theorems.natural_language_statement:
Scratch tapes: the missing notion of blank working storage in the mission's machine model.

`DecidesInPolynomialTime` on $\mathrm{Fin}\,k \to \mathrm{List\ Bool}$ supplies exactly $k$ tapes, every one preloaded with a component of the input. There is no blank work tape anywhere in the model, and nothing in the development provides one: the encoded simulation preserves the tape count, and `decidesInPolynomialTime_add_unused_tape` runs the other way, adding a tape to the *input* rather than handing out scratch.

This is a hard obstruction rather than an inconvenience. One of the mission's open frontier obligations asks for a `TypedMachine 3` that simulates a `Machine 4`, so tape multiplexing is forced by the statement itself. More broadly, without scratch one cannot even show that $\mathrm{P}$ is closed under intersection: running a second machine requires somewhere to record the first one's answer.

This module supplies the notion. `withScratch s x` pads an input tuple with $s$ empty tapes, and

$$
\mathrm{DecidesInPolynomialTimeWithScratch}\; s\; P
$$

asserts decidability of $P$ in polynomial time by a machine granted $s$ extra tapes, each of which starts empty. `decidesInPolynomialTimeWithScratch_zero` records that at $s = 0$ this collapses exactly to the mission's own `DecidesInPolynomialTime`, so the notion is a conservative extension rather than a new primitive.

The point of the definition is that it makes the obstruction addressable by a single theorem: provisioning any number of scratch tapes reduces, by induction, to eliminating one.
theorems.source: Standard multitape Turing-machine simulation (reduction of tape count with polynomial overhead), specialized to the model of Def_sipser_gacs_lautemann.

    intro input
    have h := hcorrect input
    rwa [withScratch_zero]

end SipserGacsLautemann
theorems.natural_language_statement:
Scratch tapes: the missing notion of blank working storage in the mission's machine model.

`DecidesInPolynomialTime` on $\mathrm{Fin}\,k \to \mathrm{List\ Bool}$ supplies exactly $k$ tapes, every one preloaded with a component of the input. There is no blank work tape anywhere in the model, and nothing in the development provides one: the encoded simulation preserves the tape count, and `decidesInPolynomialTime_add_unused_tape` runs the other way, adding a tape to the *input* rather than handing out scratch.

This is a hard obstruction rather than an inconvenience. One of the mission's open frontier obligations asks for a `TypedMachine 3` that simulates a `Machine 4`, so tape multiplexing is forced by the statement itself. More broadly, without scratch one cannot even show that $\mathrm{P}$ is closed under intersection: running a second machine requires somewhere to record the first one's answer.

This module supplies the notion. `withScratch s x` pads an input tuple with $s$ empty tapes, and

$$
\mathrm{DecidesInPolynomialTimeWithScratch}\; s\; P
$$

asserts decidability of $P$ in polynomial time by a machine granted $s$ extra tapes, each of which starts empty. `decidesInPolynomialTimeWithScratch_zero` records that at $s = 0$ this collapses exactly to the mission's own `DecidesInPolynomialTime`, so the notion is a conservative extension rather than a new primitive.

The point of the definition is that it makes the obstruction addressable by a single theorem: provisioning any number of scratch tapes reduces, by induction, to eliminating one.
theorems.source: Standard multitape Turing-machine simulation (reduction of tape count with polynomial overhead), specialized to the model of Def_sipser_gacs_lautemann.
theorems.theorem_title: Scratch tapes for the mission machine model

namespace SipserGacsLautemann

theorem polynomiallyBounded_mul {f g : Nat → Nat}
    (hf : PolynomiallyBounded f) (hg : PolynomiallyBounded g) :
    PolynomiallyBounded (fun n => f n * g n) := by sorry

end SipserGacsLautemann
theorems.natural_language_statement:
If $f$ and $g$ are polynomially bounded, so is their pointwise product $n \mapsto f(n) \cdot g(n)$.

Here a function $b : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is *polynomially bounded* when there exist constants $c, d \in \mathbb{N}$ with $b(n) \le c\,(n+1)^d$ for every $n$. Products are exactly what appears when a machine performs a polynomially bounded number of rounds, each of polynomially bounded cost — the shape of every simulation argument in this mission.

theorems.theorem_title: Polynomially bounded functions are closed under products

theorem ternary_majority_scheduler_reports_accepts_under_halt_bound
    (states : Nat)
    (machine : Machine 2 states)
    (depth : Nat → Nat)
    (bound : Nat → Nat)
    (hbound : PolynomiallyBounded bound)
    (hleaves : PolynomiallyBounded (fun n : Nat => 3 ^ depth n)) :
    ∃ (State : Type) (_ : Fintype State)
      (scheduler : TypedMachine 2 State)
      (schedulerTime : Nat → Nat),
      PolynomiallyBounded schedulerTime ∧
        ∀ input : Fin 2 → List Bool,
          (∀ random : List Bool,
            random.length ≤ (input 1).length →
              ∃ result : Bool,
                machine.result
                    (machine.run
                      (ternaryTwoTapeInput input random)
                      (bound (totalInputLength input))).state =
                  some result) →
          scheduler.result
              (scheduler.run input
                (schedulerTime (totalInputLength input))).state =
            some
              (let d := depth (input 0).length
               let leafCount := 3 ^ d
               let randomBits := (input 1).length / leafCount
               ternaryVoteConstruction
                 (fun random : List Bool =>
                   @decide
                    (machine.acceptsWithin
                      (ternaryTwoTapeInput input random)
                      (bound (totalInputLength input)))
                    (Classical.propDecidable _))
                 d
                 (ternaryListTreeConstruction
                   randomBits d (input 1))) := by
  sorry

end SipserGacsLautemann
theorems.natural_language_statement:
This is the ternary-majority scheduler construction with an explicit uniform halt bound.

Fix a two-tape machine $M$, a depth function $d(n)$ whose number of ternary leaves $3^{d(n)}$ is polynomially bounded, and a polynomially bounded halt bound $B(n)$. The theorem asks for a finite-state two-tape scheduler which, on input $(x,r)$, evaluates the ternary majority tree over the leaf random strings extracted from $r$.

The hypothesis for each input says that every relevant leaf query has halted by time $B(|x,r|)$. Under that hypothesis, the scheduler reports the ternary majority of the Boolean values

$$
\mathbf{1}[M \text{ accepts } (x,\rho) \text{ within } B(|x,r|) \text{ steps}]
$$

over all leaves $\rho$ in the ternary tree. This isolates the concrete scheduler/simulation construction from the separate verifier-correctness argument.

    (states : Nat)

theorems.natural_language_statement:
Let a concrete four-tape verifier machine and an explicit polynomial upper bound $C(N+1)^d$ be given. This theorem isolates the result-only machine-construction obligation for one decoded cover-shift query.

On input $(x,e,u,o)$, the scheduler computes the transformed virtual input $(x,e,u\oplus t_i,o)$, where $t_i$ is the decoded block selected by $i=\min(|o|,|u|)$, runs or simulates the supplied base machine on that virtual input up to the explicit bound $C(N+1)^d$, and reports whether the base machine accepts. Let a concrete two-tape verifier machine be given, let the ternary tree have polynomially many leaves, and fix an explicit polynomial upper bound $C(N+1)^d$ for each base-machine call. This theorem isolates the finite-state scheduler needed by ternary amplification when every leaf simulation is run to that explicit common bound.

    (verifier : List Bool → List Bool → Bool)

Let $V(x,r)$ be decided by a deterministic two-tape verifier machine in polynomial time. Given four tapes $(x,e,u,o)$, interpret the length of the fourth tape as a unary shift offset, capped at $|u|$. Decode that one translation from the encoded translation list $e$, XOR it with $u$, and run $V$ on the resulting query.

This theorem asserts that this single decoded-shift query predicate is decidable in polynomial time. It isolates the query-construction and one-call simulation part of the shifted-cover verifier scheduler.

import Definitions.Def_sgl_polynomial_closures
import Mathlib.Tactic

namespace SipserGacsLautemann

theorem linear_argument_le_scaled_succ
    (a b n : Nat) :
    a * n + b + 1 ≤ (a + b + 1) * (n + 1) := by
  have ha : a * n ≤ a * (n + 1) :=
    Nat.mul_le_mul_left a (Nat.le_succ n)
  have hb : b + 1 ≤ (b + 1) * (n + 1) := by
    have hone : 1 ≤ n + 1 := Nat.succ_pos n
    simpa using Nat.mul_le_mul_left (b + 1) hone
  calc
    a * n + b + 1 = a * n + (b + 1) := by omega
    _ ≤ a * (n + 1) + (b + 1) * (n + 1) :=
      Nat.add_le_add ha hb
    _ = (a + b + 1) * (n + 1) := by
      ring

theorem PolynomiallyBounded.comp_linear
    {f : Nat → Nat}
    (hf : PolynomiallyBounded f)
    (a b : Nat) :
    PolynomiallyBounded (fun n => f (a * n + b)) := by
  rcases hf with ⟨coefficient, degree, hbound⟩
  refine
    ⟨coefficient * (a + b + 1) ^ degree,
      degree, ?_⟩
  intro n
  have hlinear :
      a * n + b + 1 ≤
        (a + b + 1) * (n + 1) :=
    linear_argument_le_scaled_succ a b n
  have hpow :
      (a * n + b + 1) ^ degree ≤
        ((a + b + 1) * (n + 1)) ^ degree :=
    Nat.pow_le_pow_left hlinear degree
  calc
    f (a * n + b) ≤
        coefficient * (a * n + b + 1) ^ degree :=
      hbound (a * n + b)
    _ ≤ coefficient *
        ((a + b + 1) * (n + 1)) ^ degree :=
      Nat.mul_le_mul_left coefficient hpow
    _ = (coefficient * (a + b + 1) ^ degree) *
        (n + 1) ^ degree := by
      rw [Nat.mul_pow]
      ac_rfl

theorem PolynomiallyBounded.comp_add_const
    {f : Nat → Nat}
    (hf : PolynomiallyBounded f)
    (b : Nat) :
    PolynomiallyBounded (fun n => f (n + b)) := by
  simpa [Nat.one_mul] using hf.comp_linear 1 b

theorem PolynomiallyBounded.comp_mul_const
    {f : Nat → Nat}
    (hf : PolynomiallyBounded f)
    (a : Nat) :
    PolynomiallyBounded (fun n => f (a * n)) := by
  simpa using hf.comp_linear a 0

end SipserGacsLautemann
theorems.natural_language_statement:
This module proves a standard closure property for the mission predicate `PolynomiallyBounded`: if a time bound $f(n)$ is polynomially bounded, then so is $n\mapsto f(a n + b)$ for fixed natural constants $a$ and $b$. It also records the special cases of adding a constant to the input length and multiplying the input length by a constant.

This is scheduler bookkeeping for the Sipser--Gács--Lautemann machine construction: verifier-query lengths and encoded-simulation input lengths are bounded by affine functions of the controlling input lengths, so existing polynomial verifier time bounds can be transported through those size changes.
theorems.source: Standard closure of polynomially bounded functions under affine input scaling; used in the Prove2me Sipser--Gács--Lautemann scheduler formalization.
theorems.theorem_title: Polynomial bounds are closed under affine input scaling

      ring

theorem PolynomiallyBounded.comp_linear
    {f : Nat → Nat}
    (hf : PolynomiallyBounded f)
    (a b : Nat) :
    PolynomiallyBounded (fun n => f (a * n + b)) := by
  rcases hf with ⟨coefficient, degree, hbound⟩
  refine
    ⟨coefficient * (a + b + 1) ^ degree,
      degree, ?_⟩
  intro n
  have hlinear :
      a * n + b + 1 ≤
        (a + b + 1) * (n + 1) :=
    linear_argument_le_scaled_succ a b n
  have hpow :
      (a * n + b + 1) ^ degree ≤
        ((a + b + 1) * (n + 1)) ^ degree :=
    Nat.pow_le_pow_left hlinear degree
  calc
    f (a * n + b) ≤
        coefficient * (a * n + b + 1) ^ degree :=
      hbound (a * n + b)
    _ ≤ coefficient *
        ((a + b + 1) * (n + 1)) ^ degree :=
      Nat.mul_le_mul_left coefficient hpow
    _ = (coefficient * (a + b + 1) ^ degree) *
        (n + 1) ^ degree := by
      rw [Nat.mul_pow]
      ac_rfl

theorem PolynomiallyBounded.comp_add_const
    {f : Nat → Nat}
    (hf : PolynomiallyBounded f)
    (b : Nat) :
    PolynomiallyBounded (fun n => f (n + b)) := by
  simpa [Nat.one_mul] using hf.comp_linear 1 b

theorem PolynomiallyBounded.comp_mul_const
    {f : Nat → Nat}
    (hf : PolynomiallyBounded f)
    (a : Nat) :
    PolynomiallyBounded (fun n => f (a * n)) := by
  simpa using hf.comp_linear a 0

namespace SipserGacsLautemann

theorem moveLeftPrefixTypedMachine_iterate_embedded
    {tapes : Nat} {State : Type}
    (machine : TypedMachine tapes State)
    (configuration : TypedConfiguration tapes State)
    (steps : Nat) :
    ((moveLeftPrefixTypedMachine machine).step^[steps])
        (MoveLeftPrefixState.embedConfiguration configuration) =
      MoveLeftPrefixState.embedConfiguration
        ((machine.step^[steps]) configuration) := by
  induction steps with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ steps ih =>
      rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply',
        Function.iterate_succ_apply', ih]
      exact moveLeftPrefixTypedMachine_step_running
        machine ((machine.step^[steps]) configuration)

theorem moveLeftPrefixTypedMachine_reaches_embedded
    {tapes : Nat} {State : Type}
    (machine : TypedMachine tapes State)
    {initial final : TypedConfiguration tapes State}
    {bound : Nat}
    (hreaches :
      ReachesWithin machine.step initial final bound) :
    ReachesWithin
      (moveLeftPrefixTypedMachine machine).step
      (MoveLeftPrefixState.embedConfiguration initial)
      (MoveLeftPrefixState.embedConfiguration final)
      bound := by
  rcases hreaches with ⟨steps, hle, hsteps⟩
  refine ⟨steps, hle, ?_⟩
  rw [moveLeftPrefixTypedMachine_iterate_embedded, hsteps]

theorem moveLeftPrefixTypedMachine_result_embedded
    {tapes : Nat} {State : Type}
    (machine : TypedMachine tapes State)
    (configuration : TypedConfiguration tapes State) :
    (moveLeftPrefixTypedMachine machine).result
        (MoveLeftPrefixState.embedConfiguration configuration).state =
      machine.result configuration.state := by
  rfl

theorem leftZigzagReadyConfiguration_result
    {baseStates : Nat}
    (baseMachine : Machine 2 baseStates)
    (configuration : Configuration 2 baseStates)
    (archives : Fin 2 → List TapeSymbol)
    (positions : Fin 2 → Int)
    (recordCount : Nat) :
    (leftZigzagSimulationTypedMachine baseMachine).result
        (leftZigzagReadyConfiguration
          configuration archives positions recordCount).state =
      baseMachine.result configuration.state := by
  rfl

theorem leftZigzagSimulation_reaches_run_with_result
    {baseStates : Nat}
    (baseMachine : Machine 2 baseStates)
    (input : Fin 2 → List Bool)
    (archives : Fin 2 → List TapeSymbol)
    (steps horizon : Nat)
    (hsteps : steps ≤ horizon) :
    ∃ final : TypedConfiguration 2
        (ZigzagSimulationState baseStates),
      ReachesWithin
        (leftZigzagSimulationTypedMachine baseMachine).step
        (leftZigzagReadyConfiguration
          (baseMachine.run input 0) archives
          (zigzagRunPositions baseMachine input 0)
          (2 * horizon + 3))
        final
        (steps * (24 * horizon + 32)) ∧
      (leftZigzagSimulationTypedMachine baseMachine).result
          final.state =
        baseMachine.result
          (baseMachine.run input steps).state := by
  refine
    ⟨leftZigzagReadyConfiguration
        (baseMachine.run input steps) archives
        (zigzagRunPositions baseMachine input steps)
        (2 * horizon + 3),
      leftZigzagSimulation_reaches_run
        baseMachine input archives steps horizon hsteps,
      ?_⟩
  exact
    leftZigzagReadyConfiguration_result
      baseMachine (baseMachine.run input steps)
      archives (zigzagRunPositions baseMachine input steps)
      (2 * horizon + 3)

end SipserGacsLautemann
theorems.natural_language_statement:
This module packages result-readout and reachability adapters for the Sipser--Gács--Lautemann simulator stack. It lifts `ReachesWithin` proofs through the move-left prefix when the prefixed machine is already in an embedded running state, records that embedded prefixed states have the same result as the underlying typed machine, and records that a completed left-zigzag simulation reads out exactly the result of the simulated base machine run.

These lemmas are intended for the remaining aggregation scheduler: after a loader constructs a ready verifier-query configuration, these adapters let the proof append the verifier simulation phase and recover the Boolean answer with the published polynomial-overhead bound.

import Definitions.Def_sgl_raw_archive_machine
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Sum

namespace SipserGacsLautemann

inductive MoveLeftPrefixState (State : Type) where
  | moveLeft
  | running : State → MoveLeftPrefixState State
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

def moveLeftInitialConfiguration
    {tapes : Nat} {State : Type}
    (machine : TypedMachine tapes State)
    (input : Fin tapes → List Bool) :
    TypedConfiguration tapes State where
  state := machine.start
  tape := fun i => (Tape.ofBits (input i)).move .left

def MoveLeftPrefixState.embedConfiguration
    {tapes : Nat} {State : Type}
    (configuration : TypedConfiguration tapes State) :
    TypedConfiguration tapes (MoveLeftPrefixState State) where
  state := .running configuration.state
  tape := configuration.tape

def moveLeftPrefixTypedMachine
    {tapes : Nat} {State : Type}
    (machine : TypedMachine tapes State) :
    TypedMachine tapes (MoveLeftPrefixState State) where
  start := .moveLeft
  transition state symbols :=
    match state with
    | .moveLeft =>
        (.running machine.start,
          fun i => (symbols i, .left))
    | .running baseState =>
        let action := machine.transition baseState symbols
        (.running action.1, action.2)
  result
    | .moveLeft => none
    | .running baseState => machine.result baseState

theorem moveLeftPrefixTypedMachine_step_running
    {tapes : Nat} {State : Type}
    (machine : TypedMachine tapes State)
    (configuration : TypedConfiguration tapes State) :
    (moveLeftPrefixTypedMachine machine).step
        (MoveLeftPrefixState.embedConfiguration configuration) =
      MoveLeftPrefixState.embedConfiguration
        (machine.step configuration) := by
  cases configuration with
  | mk state tape =>
      cases hresult : machine.result state with
      | some result =>
          simp [TypedMachine.step,
            moveLeftPrefixTypedMachine,
            MoveLeftPrefixState.embedConfiguration,
            hresult]
      | none =>
          simp [TypedMachine.step,
            moveLeftPrefixTypedMachine,
            MoveLeftPrefixState.embedConfiguration,
            hresult]

theorem moveLeftPrefixTypedMachine_run_one
    {tapes : Nat} {State : Type}
    (machine : TypedMachine tapes State)
    (input : Fin tapes → List Bool) :
    (moveLeftPrefixTypedMachine machine).run input 1 =
      MoveLeftPrefixState.embedConfiguration
        (moveLeftInitialConfiguration machine input) := by
  rfl

theorem moveLeftPrefixTypedMachine_run_succ
    {tapes : Nat} {State : Type}
    (machine : TypedMachine tapes State)
    (input : Fin tapes → List Bool)
    (steps : Nat) :
    (moveLeftPrefixTypedMachine machine).run input
        (steps + 1) =
      MoveLeftPrefixState.embedConfiguration
        ((machine.step^[steps])
          (moveLeftInitialConfiguration machine input)) := by
  induction steps with
  | zero =>
      exact moveLeftPrefixTypedMachine_run_one machine input
  | succ steps ih =>
      change
        (moveLeftPrefixTypedMachine machine).run input
            ((steps + 1) + 1) =
          MoveLeftPrefixState.embedConfiguration
            ((machine.step^[steps + 1])
              (moveLeftInitialConfiguration machine input))
      rw [TypedMachine.run, ih]
      rw [moveLeftPrefixTypedMachine_step_running]
      rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply']

theorem moveLeftPrefixTypedMachine_result_run_succ
    {tapes : Nat} {State : Type}
    (machine : TypedMachine tapes State)
    (input : Fin tapes → List Bool)
    (steps : Nat) :
    (moveLeftPrefixTypedMachine machine).result
        ((moveLeftPrefixTypedMachine machine).run input
          (steps + 1)).state =
      machine.result
        (((machine.step^[steps])
          (moveLeftInitialConfiguration machine input)).state) := by
  rw [moveLeftPrefixTypedMachine_run_succ]
  rfl

end SipserGacsLautemann

import Definitions.Def_sipser_gacs_lautemann

namespace SipserGacsLautemann

theorem Machine.step_eq_self_of_result_eq_some
    {tapes states : Nat}
    (machine : Machine tapes states)
    (configuration : Configuration tapes states)
    {result : Bool}
    (hresult : machine.result configuration.state = some result) :
    machine.step configuration = configuration := by
  simp [Machine.step, hresult]

theorem Machine.run_add_of_result_eq_some
    {tapes states : Nat}
    (machine : Machine tapes states)
    (input : Fin tapes → List Bool)
    (steps extra : Nat)
    {result : Bool}
    (hresult :
      machine.result (machine.run input steps).state =
        some result) :
    machine.run input (steps + extra) =
      machine.run input steps := by
  induction extra with
  | zero => simp
  | succ extra ih =>
      rw [Nat.add_succ, Machine.run, ih]
      exact
        machine.step_eq_self_of_result_eq_some
          (machine.run input steps) hresult

theorem Machine.acceptsWithin_mono_steps
    {tapes states : Nat}
    (machine : Machine tapes states)
    (input : Fin tapes → List Bool)
    {earlier later : Nat}
    (hle : earlier ≤ later)
    (haccepts : machine.acceptsWithin input earlier) :
    machine.acceptsWithin input later := by
  obtain ⟨extra, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hle
  unfold Machine.acceptsWithin at haccepts ⊢
  rw [machine.run_add_of_result_eq_some
    input earlier extra haccepts]
  exact haccepts

theorem Machine.rejectsWithin_mono_steps
    {tapes states : Nat}
    (machine : Machine tapes states)
    (input : Fin tapes → List Bool)
    {earlier later : Nat}
    (hle : earlier ≤ later)
    (hrejects : machine.rejectsWithin input earlier) :
    machine.rejectsWithin input later := by
  obtain ⟨extra, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hle
  unfold Machine.rejectsWithin at hrejects ⊢
  rw [machine.run_add_of_result_eq_some
    input earlier extra hrejects]
  exact hrejects

theorem Machine.not_accepts_and_rejects_same_time
    {tapes states : Nat}
    (machine : Machine tapes states)
    (input : Fin tapes → List Bool)
    (steps : Nat) :
    ¬ (machine.acceptsWithin input steps ∧
        machine.rejectsWithin input steps) := by
  intro hboth
  rcases hboth with ⟨haccepts, hrejects⟩
  unfold Machine.acceptsWithin at haccepts
  unfold Machine.rejectsWithin at hrejects
  rw [haccepts] at hrejects
  cases hrejects

end SipserGacsLautemann

import Definitions.Def_sipser_gacs_lautemann
import Mathlib.Tactic

namespace SipserGacsLautemann

theorem PolynomiallyBounded.const (constant : Nat) :
    PolynomiallyBounded (fun _ : Nat => constant) := by
  refine ⟨constant, 0, ?_⟩
  intro n
  simp

theorem PolynomiallyBounded.id :
    PolynomiallyBounded (fun n : Nat => n) := by
  refine ⟨1, 1, ?_⟩
  intro n
  simp

theorem PolynomiallyBounded.add {f g : Nat → Nat}
    (hf : PolynomiallyBounded f) (hg : PolynomiallyBounded g) :
    PolynomiallyBounded (fun n => f n + g n) := by
  rcases hf with ⟨cf, df, hfbound⟩
  rcases hg with ⟨cg, dg, hgbound⟩
  refine ⟨cf + cg, df + dg, ?_⟩
  intro n
  let base := n + 1
  have hbase : 1 ≤ base := Nat.succ_pos n
  have hdf :
      base ^ df ≤ base ^ (df + dg) :=
    Nat.pow_le_pow_right hbase (Nat.le_add_right df dg)
  have hdg :
      base ^ dg ≤ base ^ (df + dg) :=
    Nat.pow_le_pow_right hbase (Nat.le_add_left dg df)
  calc
    f n + g n ≤ cf * base ^ df + cg * base ^ dg :=
      Nat.add_le_add (hfbound n) (hgbound n)
    _ ≤ cf * base ^ (df + dg) +
          cg * base ^ (df + dg) := by
      exact
        Nat.add_le_add
          (Nat.mul_le_mul_left cf hdf)
          (Nat.mul_le_mul_left cg hdg)
    _ = (cf + cg) * base ^ (df + dg) := by
      rw [Nat.add_mul]

theorem PolynomiallyBounded.mul {f g : Nat → Nat}
    (hf : PolynomiallyBounded f) (hg : PolynomiallyBounded g) :
    PolynomiallyBounded (fun n => f n * g n) := by
  rcases hf with ⟨cf, df, hfbound⟩
  rcases hg with ⟨cg, dg, hgbound⟩
  refine ⟨cf * cg, df + dg, ?_⟩
  intro n
  let base := n + 1
  calc
    f n * g n ≤
        (cf * base ^ df) * (cg * base ^ dg) :=
      Nat.mul_le_mul (hfbound n) (hgbound n)
    _ = (cf * cg) * base ^ (df + dg) := by
      rw [Nat.pow_add]
      ac_rfl

theorem PolynomiallyBounded.const_mul {f : Nat → Nat}
    (constant : Nat) (hf : PolynomiallyBounded f) :
    PolynomiallyBounded (fun n => constant * f n) := by
  exact (PolynomiallyBounded.const constant).mul hf

theorem PolynomiallyBounded.mul_const {f : Nat → Nat}
    (hf : PolynomiallyBounded f) (constant : Nat) :
    PolynomiallyBounded (fun n => f n * constant) := by
  simpa [Nat.mul_comm] using hf.mul (PolynomiallyBounded.const constant)

theorem PolynomiallyBounded.pow_const {f : Nat → Nat}
    (hf : PolynomiallyBounded f) :
    ∀ exponent : Nat,
      PolynomiallyBounded (fun n => (f n) ^ exponent)
  | 0 => by
      simpa using PolynomiallyBounded.const 1
  | exponent + 1 => by
      simpa [Nat.pow_succ] using
        (PolynomiallyBounded.pow_const hf exponent).mul hf

theorem PolynomiallyBounded.succ {f : Nat → Nat}
    (hf : PolynomiallyBounded f) :
    PolynomiallyBounded (fun n => f n + 1) := by
  simpa using hf.add (PolynomiallyBounded.const 1)

end SipserGacsLautemann

theorems.natural_language_statement:
Let $V(x,r)$ be a Boolean predicate decided in polynomial time by the mission's deterministic two-tape Turing-machine model. Given an input $x$, an encoded list of translations $e$, and a universal string $u$, decode $|u|+1$ translations $t_0,\ldots,t_{|u|}$ of width $|u|$. Then the shifted-cover predicate

$$
C_V(x,e,u)=\bigvee_{i=0}^{|u|} V\bigl(x,u\mathbin{\oplus}t_i\bigr)
$$

is decidable in polynomial time. Bits outside the supplied encoding are read as zero, exactly as prescribed by the mission's decoding function.

This is the computational closure lemma for the Lautemann-cover half of the Sipser–Gács–Lautemann formalization. It requires only $|u|+1$ simulations of the verifier machine, plus polynomial-time decoding and bitwise exclusive-or.

**Formalization Note** The decoded translations and existential test are exactly `decodeCoverTranslationConstruction` and `coverVerifierConstruction`.

theorems.natural_language_statement:
Let $V(x,r)$ be a Boolean predicate decided in polynomial time by the mission's deterministic two-tape Turing-machine model. For an input $x$, put

$$
d=\left\lceil\log_2(|x|+1)\right\rceil+3.
$$

Split the supplied random string into $3^d$ padded blocks of equal inferred width, evaluate $V(x,\cdot)$ on every block, and combine those values with the complete depth-$d$ ternary tree whose internal gate is majority-of-three. The resulting predicate

$$
A_V(x,\rho)=\operatorname{Maj}_3^{(d)}\bigl(V(x,r_1),\ldots,V(x,r_{3^d})\bigr)
$$

is decidable in polynomial time.

This is the computational closure lemma for the amplification half of the Sipser–Gács–Lautemann formalization. The number of oracle-machine simulations is polynomial because $3^d$ is polynomial in $|x|$, and each inferred block has length at most $|\rho|$.

**Formalization Note** The block padding, ternary reshaping, recursive vote, and depth are exactly `ternaryAmplifiedVerifierConstruction` and its published helper definitions.
